metadata.dataset: USFWS National Wetlands Inventory along the full Minnesota North Country Trail — 2-mile corridor, classified GO / MAYBE / NO-GO for trail routing
metadata.corridor: Statewide NCT line (site/data/trail-minnesota.geojson, 348 features) buffered 2 mi (3,218.69 m); a wetland counts when its polygon intersects the buffer
metadata.service_note: Task brief named the fws.gov MapServer URL; it returns 404 — the service moved to ArcGIS Online (this URL). The DNR's own updated-NWI service is token-gated (499) and not publicly queryable. Minnesota content in the national file is the DNR June 2019 update delivered to FWS. Per-polygon vintage is NOT exposed by this service — recorded as a limit.
metadata.classification: Rules W1-W10 / C1-C4 from the Nov 18 2026 classification sweep (research_notes/nwi-wetland-trail-classification-20261118-1744/report.md). GO is absence of a polygon (W1) — no GO features exist in this file. The GO/MAYBE/NO-GO mapping is chapter policy: no published Cowardin matrix exists; every judgment is labelled in the feature's rule field.
metadata.open_gaps: W2 overlay (DNR public waters, calcareous fen, MBS rare natural community) NOT applied — NWI alone cannot identify these and the viewer has no public-waters / Natural Heritage layer yet. W10 cumulative MAYBE length (>~1/2 mi) is a route-level rule, not a polygon rule.
metadata.simplification: Server-side maxAllowableOffset 0.0002 (~22 m) + geometryPrecision 5; measured 2026-11-18: 200-feature Itasca sample 1,614,232 bytes raw -> 51,953 bytes, 0 empty geometries, smallest polygon 856 m2 intact. Dissolved into connected components per (rating, Cowardin code).
metadata.note: Do NOT use the county wetlands.zip (46.4 MB, 2017 vintage) — flagged STALE in the Nov 11 useful-layers doc. NWI is a screening layer, not a delineation: identification ~90%, classification ~75%, 95% of features within +/-5.9 m; TMU 0.5 ac. Field delineation + permits before any MAYBE becomes a route.
